lines.say: Animals are multicellular eukaryotes that eat other organisms. Their cells have no walls.
The embryo forms a hollow ball called a blastula.
Then in gastrulation, cells move inwards to form layers.
Hox genes control the identity of body regions from head to tail.
Sponges have no true tissues. All other animals do.
Radial symmetry: many planes through a central axis give mirror halves.

draw.alt: Radial animal with many planes of symmetry

lines.say: It suits animals that drift or stay put, meeting the world from all sides.
Bilateral symmetry: only one plane gives left and right halves.

draw.alt: Bilateral animal with one plane and a head at the front

lines.say: Bilateral animals move in one direction. Sense organs gather at the front. That's cephalisation.
Sea stars look radial, but their larvae are bilateral.
Ecto is exit, the outside. It makes skin and the nervous system.
Endo is enter, the inside. It lines the gut and makes the liver.
Meso is middle. It makes muscle, most organs, skeleton and blood.
Two layers is diploblastic, like jellyfish. Three is triploblastic.
A coelom is fully lined by mesoderm. A pseudocoelom only partly.
Flatworms are acoelomates. Body cavity describes structure, not relatedness.
The blastopore is the first opening into the primitive gut.
In protostomes, the blastopore becomes the mouth. First mouth.

draw.alt: Blastopore becomes mouth in protostomes, anus in deuterostomes

lines.say: In deuterostomes, it becomes the anus. You're a deuterostome.
Deuterostome cleavage is radial and indeterminate. Coelom by enterocoely.
Indeterminate cleavage is why identical twins are possible.
Protostomes split into Lophotrochozoa and Ecdysozoa, the moulters.
Cnidarians are radial and diploblastic, with stinging cells.
Annelids are segmented worms with a coelom. Molluscs have a foot and mantle.
Arthropods have jointed legs and a chitin exoskeleton. They're the biggest phylum.
Chordates: Never Do Pigs Talk. Notochord, dorsal nerve cord, pharyngeal slits, tail.

draw.alt: Chordate features on a simple body

items.text: nerve cord on top, notochord below

lines.say: Semelparity means breeding once, then dying, like the male antechinus.
Iteroparity means breeding again and again, like most mammals.
Energy is limited, so there are trade-offs. More offspring means less care each.
I live long, two steady, three die young.

draw.alt: Survivorship curves Type I, II and III

lines.say: Species X lost 95 percent in year one. That's Type three.
Diploblastic means two germ layers, not two cells thick.
Semelparous species often make huge numbers of offspring in one go.
Classify in order: tissues, symmetry, germ layers, development, then phylum.
